title: Haiku handoff on CLI retry -- delegate mechanical CLI retries to Haiku after 2 failures
desc: After two same-kind failures on a mechanical CLI call (suggest/skill add/edit/mail/git commit with arg or validation errors), stop retrying inline on Sonnet/Opus and spawn a Haiku agent. Saves tokens and surfaces validator bugs faster. Brief must include exact cmd, verbatim error, goal, and 3 skill refs.
steps: Trigger: a mechanical CLI call (wkappbot suggest, wkappbot skill add/edit, wkappbot file edit, wkappbot mail send, git commit -m, shell-arg-heavy task) fails on a SECOND attempt with the same KIND of error (validation, parsing, encoding, quoting, arg-mangling). One failure is acceptable; two means the current model is debugging the wrong layer.
Stop retrying inline. Spawn a Haiku agent in the SAME message: Agent(model:haiku, subagent_type:general-purpose, prompt:<self-contained brief>). Do NOT loop a third time on Sonnet/Opus.

Brief MUST include: (a) exact command verbatim, (b) verbatim stderr from last attempt, (c) goal/success criteria, (d) authorization to inspect skills and reshape args, (e) 3 wkappbot skill read refs per agent-brief-guard.

Examples of mechanical (DELEGATE): wkappbot suggest with --requirement validation rejections; wkappbot skill add/edit with multi-line --steps; cmd.exe mangling; git commit messages with special chars; CLI flag combos; CP949/UTF-8 encoding clashes in argv.

Examples of NOT mechanical (HANDLE YOURSELF): architecture decisions, code review, writing the SPEC for the spawned Haiku, merging suggestions, irreversible actions like email send/git push/force-reset.

Why this saves tokens: a 4-retry suggest loop on Sonnet/Opus burns thousands of context tokens. Haiku does validation-debug loops at ~10% the rate AND is good at pattern-matching 'error said X but doc says Y' that surfaces real validator bugs.

After Haiku reports: capture the working command + validation surprise; if the validator was actually wrong/unhelpful, promote it to a fresh wkappbot suggest BUG report so the next person does not relearn it.

Real-world precedent (2026-05-29): wkappbot suggest IMPL-GUIDE submit failed 4x on Sonnet (unknown subcommand 'codex' in requirement → multi-line cmd parse fail → proposed: prefix fix). A Haiku agent would have tried proposed: on attempt 2.

requirements.cmd: Agent spawned with exact cmd, verbatim stderr, goal, 3 skill refs
requirements.expect: skill read works on all 3 refs

requirements.cmd: Haiku agent returns working command or identified validator bug
